transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’ve been forgetting things I really shouldn’t. Appointments, like heart follow-ups, forgetting to call the clinic back… even showing up to fix something and not bringing the right tools. It’s been causing problems.
When did you first notice you were having these memory problems?

Probably… a little over a year now. Maybe about a year and two months. It got more noticeable after that heart scare, when I had to cut back on walking and the projects I used to do. That’s when it started causing real trouble.
Are you having trouble with daily activities because of these memory problems?

Yeah… some. The repair group at the senior center, they can’t really count on me like they used to. And the doctor’s office has had to keep after me about heart follow-ups I missed. So… yes, it’s gotten in the way.
Do you ever feel confused or disoriented?
Not really… I mean, I don’t think I get disoriented. I know where I am and what I’m doing, mostly. It’s more like… I just don’t always keep track of things.
Have you been having trouble learning new things?
I’m not sure. I don’t really try to learn many new things these days. If it’s something simple, I think I can manage, but… I haven’t noticed a big problem there.
Have you been having any trouble with speaking or finding the right words?
Not that I’ve noticed. I mean, sometimes I pause, but I think that’s normal. I can usually say what I mean.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed lately?
I don’t know… not really sad, I guess. I have my off days, but I wouldn’t say depressed.
Do you have trouble paying attention or focusing on things?

Yeah… sometimes. Like if I’m at the bridge table, or one of those Fix-It Friends meetings, I start out meaning to listen, but after a while my mind kind of drifts. Then I realize I’ve missed a good bit of what people said.
Have you noticed any changes in your personality over the past year?
I don’t think so. I mean… I feel like I’m still pretty much myself. Nothing big that I’ve noticed.
Have you been feeling anxious or overly worried about things lately?
Not especially, no. I worry about the usual things, I suppose, but I haven’t felt overly anxious lately.
Have you needed more help from others to manage your daily life over the past year?

A little, I guess. I still manage most things, but… the repair group at the senior center can’t really count on me like they used to. And my doctor’s office has had to call after me about heart follow-ups I missed.
Have you noticed any significant decline in your memory over the past year, beyond just forgetting appointments or tools?
Not really, no. I mean, I misplace things and miss things sometimes, but I haven’t noticed my memory getting worse in some big way.
Do you have trouble figuring out how to solve problems or make decisions?
I’m not sure. I mean, I can usually decide things if I take a minute. I haven’t really noticed a big problem there.
Have you been having trouble with understanding what others are saying?
No… I don’t think so. I can follow what people are saying most of the time.
Do you have trouble planning things out, like making a schedule for the day?
I don’t really make much of a schedule, honestly. I just kind of go through the day. I haven’t noticed it being a big problem.
Have you noticed any significant decline in your ability to think and understand things over the past year?
No, I don’t think so. Nothing that stands out to me, anyway.
Have you withdrawn from social activities or stopped doing things you used to enjoy?
No… not really. I mean, I still do the usual things. I haven’t noticed pulling away from people or anything like that.
Do you have trouble with reading or understanding written information?
Not really, no. I mean, I can read things fine for the most part. I haven’t noticed a problem understanding it.
Have you noticed any significant decline in your memory for recent events or learning new information?
I haven’t really noticed anything like that. I mean, I forget little things here and there, but nothing that feels like a big decline.
Do you have trouble remembering things that happened recently, like yesterday or last week?
Not really. I mean… I might forget little odds and ends, but I don’t think I’m forgetting whole days or things from last week.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with symptoms of forgetfulness, particularly with appointments and tasks, which have caused problems in daily life. The onset of these symptoms was around a year and two months ago, and they have been persistent. While the patient does not report significant declines in other cognitive areas such as learning new things, speaking, or understanding, the prominent complaint of forgetfulness and its impact on daily functioning aligns most closely with a diagnosis of Unspecified neurocognitive disorder (R41.0). Other options like Mild neurocognitive disorder due to known physiological condition (G31.84) were considered but the information provided does not specify a clear physiological cause for the cognitive decline.
